doc.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998

title: Writing the book, advice, and his luck in a career
summary: He needs to write his book, gives career advice, and reflects on luck from Stearns's collection to Columbia.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Well that’s a good question because the near future for years has been write the God damn book. I have friends who send me big printouts from their computers, WRITE THAT BOOK and I have it on the wall. But the trouble is it’s so hard, interruptions constantly and I’m always being asked to help people. Last night the waitress at the place where I went with the guys from Colgate was a very sweet, attractive girl, and I guess she found out who I was, and she asked me for guidance on her own career which was as a singer/ guitarist, and she’s a member of a little group, her husband is the lead guitarist and so on, and I said, “Gee, it’s impossible to give advice to anyone just bang like that, I don’t know what you’re doing.” I can imagine what it is, and it’s not my area anyway, but I was able to give her one piece of advice which sounds rather routine but it works: do what you want to do the best that you can, and get as much exposure as you can and stick to it. And it’s really the best advice you can give anybody who is a performer. And it sounds simplistic but what else can you do when you start out? That’s how everybody starts out. And looking at my own life I’m amazed that I was so lucky to be an enthusiastic fan who suddenly got to hear the whole history of the music that he had gotten interested in in high school, because Marshall Stearns had one of the world’s great record collections, even though it fit into a closet, there weren’t that many records. And then I was lucky enough to be writing and get a reputation that persuaded Columbia Records to ask me, a student, to go the 23 miles or so from New Haven to Bridgeport where the factory was and research the material for the series. And it just went on like that. To be in the right place at the right time, and also to be working the best you can at what you’re interested in and suddenly create a career. I never thought I’d be in the music business but there I was. I wanted to be an English teacher.
We’re glad you were and are still.
So I hope you find some time for that book.
